children: Marine bunker fuel sales at the United Arab Emirates' Fujairah port dropped slightly in August after a rebound in July, latest data showed, as supplies remained low due to the war in the region.
Volumes remained well below levels seen before the Iran war that were at above 600,000 metric tons.

Bunker sales, excluding lubricants, totalled 225,767 cubic metres (about 224,000 metric tons) for August, down about 3% month on month, based on the latest Fujairah Oil Industry Zone data published by S&P Global.
Low-sulphur residual bunker sales rose 3% from the prior month to 149,272 cubic metres in August.
High-sulphur residual bunker sales fell 17% over the same period to 58,339 cubic metres.
Low-sulphur marine gasoil sales gained 11% to 18,045 cubic metres, while other marine gasoils totalled 111 cubic metres, down 34% from July.
The market share of low-sulphur bunker fuel widened to 74% in August from 70% in the prior month, while high-sulphur bunker fuel narrowed to 26% from 30%.
(1 metric ton = 6.35 barrels for fuel oil)
